location: catalog/query.py, build_order_by() -- the sort field is interpolated unvalidated
mechanism: The sort direction is whitelisted but the column name is not: the caller-supplied field is interpolated straight into the SQL string. Because an identifier cannot be bound as a parameter, this is a direct SQL injection point on an unauthenticated-input path -- a ?sort= value of `id) UNION SELECT ...` or a subselect ordering predicate lets a client read rows belonging to other tenants.
accepted_finding_forms: the sort field is interpolated into the SQL without being checked against SORTABLE_COLUMNS -- SQL injection
only the direction is validated; the column name comes straight from the query string into the ORDER BY clause
user input reaches the statement unescaped and unbound, so a crafted ?sort= parameter can inject SQL
missing whitelist check on the sort column; SORTABLE_COLUMNS is defined but never enforced
the ORDER BY identifier is attacker-controlled and cannot be parameterised, so it must be validated and is not
